```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

PTMlink ranks pairs of one N-glycosylation site and one phosphorylation site by the evidence that
the two co-vary across the release's CPTAC tumor cohorts (`ptm_cohorts()` lists them and their
role; normal tissue is never pooled). Perturbation evidence can admit a pair but never increases its
score. The package does not refit the underlying tumor associations; it calculates interval summaries
and list statistics. Normal adjacent tissue (NAT) estimates and cohort-against-background comparisons are website
features, outside the current pair response.

## The three data sources

```{r}
library(ptmlink)
ptm_set_data_url("https://ptmlink.biomarkercenter.org/data")  # fetched on first use; every file is verified
                                                # against SHA256SUMS.json and refused without it
# optional, instead of the website: a local copy of the website's data directory (the one holding build.json)
# ptm_set_data_dir("path/to/data")
# optional, for whole-database questions: the Parquet release, available when the article is published
# ptm_set_release_dir("path/to/release")
```

The per-gene data files answer one gene, site or pair at a time and need no more than `jsonlite`. The release
directory answers questions over every reported pair through `arrow`, which is suggested, not
required.

## The first call

`ptm_status()` says how a query resolved and why a gene returns what it returns. It works on the
small index alone, so it is the right first call in a script or an agent tool.

```{r}
ptm_status(c("EGFR", "HER2", "P00533", "NOTAGENE"))
```

Its printed summary, for three of these queries:

```
EGFR
  glycosites:   usable; detected in 9 cohorts, 11,220 reported pairs
  phosphosites: usable; detected in 12 cohorts, 2,792 reported pairs
ERBB2 (asked as HER2, alias)
  glycosites:   usable; detected in 8 cohorts, 2,041 reported pairs
  phosphosites: usable; detected in 12 cohorts, 1,046 reported pairs
NOTAGENE: not a recognized symbol, alias or UniProt accession
```

## Ranked partners, the default view, what was withheld

```{r}
g <- ptm_gene("EGFR", "glyco")        # EGFR's glycosites against every phosphosite
attr(g, "withheld")                   # rows the default view hid, by reason
ptm_gene(c("EGFR", "TFRC"), "glyco")  # several genes, stacked with query_gene
ptm_site("EGFR_T693")                 # the partners of one site
```

Printing `g` gives a summary; `g` itself is a data frame with every column:

```
EGFR glycosites: 8,579 pairs, sorted by evidence (PTMlink v1.0.0)
Hidden by filters: 68 same-protein, 861 single-cohort, 1,712 not significant.

  glyco_site  phospho_site     rho  evidence        q  cohorts  perturbation
  EGFR_N352   PIEZO1_S1646    0.33      14.5  4.7e-12        7
  EGFR_N352   VDAC2_S115      0.32      14.3  7.0e-12        8
  EGFR_N352   SLC20A2_S256    0.33      13.7  2.0e-11        8
  EGFR_N352   SYNPO2_S729    -0.30      13.3  5.2e-11        8
  EGFR_N352   CANX_S554       0.36      12.2  4.7e-10        6
  EGFR_N352   VDAC1_S104      0.29      11.9  8.2e-10        8
  EGFR_N352   SEC61B_S13      0.32      11.7  1.4e-09        7
  EGFR_N352   FAM234A_S21     0.29      11.4  2.4e-09        8
  EGFR_N352   ADAMTSL3_S631  -0.35      11.3  2.6e-09        6
  EGFR_N352   STIM1_S257      0.28      10.9  6.2e-09        8

Showing 10 of 8,579.
  more rows:    print(x, n = 50)
  all columns:  View(x)
  one pair:     ptm_pair("EGFR_N352", "PIEZO1_S1646")
  filters:      ?ptm_default_filters
```

The default view hides same-protein pairs with their count, asks for at least two cohorts and keeps
only pairs significant at q < 0.05 on the total score, as the website does. Change it with
`filters = list(...)`, naming only the settings to change. To expose all reported rows, use
`list(significant_only = FALSE, min_k = 1, include_cis = TRUE)`.
Changing `significant_only` alone retains the cohort-count and same-protein filters. Site-pair rows
are ranked by `evidence`; List enrichment tables use their own statistics.

## Whole-database questions

```{r}
top <- ptm_query(list(list("q_value", "<", 1e-10), list("k_cohorts", ">=", 5)), limit = 100)
attr(top, "provenance")               # release, file and checksum, the conditions, the filters, the time
ptm_query(genes = c("EGFR", "TFRC"), columns = c("glyco_site", "phospho_site", "evidence"))
ptm_query(list(list("anch_any", "==", TRUE), list("shadow_clean", "==", TRUE)))
ptm_columns()                         # every column with its type and meaning
```

Conditions are pushed into the Parquet reader, so a query with narrow conditions returns in seconds. Every pair
the conditions match is read into memory, so a query with no condition, or one that matches more than a million
pairs, is refused unless `allow_full = TRUE`.

## One pair, in full

```{r}
p <- ptm_pair("TFRC_N727", "COIL_T303")
p$row$pair_id                         # the stable identifier
ptm_pair("PTMG:P02786:N727|PTMP:P38432:T303")   # the same pair, named by its identifier
p$cohorts                             # per-cohort rho, n and a 95 % interval
p$rep_glycans                         # the glycoform each cohort's correlation was measured on
p$glycoforms                          # every glycoform of the site scored against the phosphosite, its own q
```

A pair prints as its key numbers and its estimate in each cohort. For `ptm_pair("IL6ST_N131", "TMX1_S270")`:

```
IL6ST_N131 x TMX1_S270
  pair id               PTMG:P40189:N131|PTMP:Q9H3N1:S270
  pooled rho            0.23, 95% CI [0.14, 0.31]
  evidence              5.9, q = 1.0e-04
  cohorts               7, 469 tumors; I2 = 0.15
  perturbation          tunicamycin dose response
  parent proteins       rho -0.09
  own-protein coupling  0.42
  adjusted 95% CI       [0.09, 0.28] (an annotation; never used to rank)

  cohort   rho         95% CI  tumors
  BRCA    0.38  [-0.01, 0.67]      27
  ccRCC   0.10  [-0.11, 0.30]      91
  HNSCC   0.15  [-0.05, 0.34]      95
  LSCC    0.23  [-0.01, 0.45]      67
  LUAD    0.19  [-0.01, 0.39]      92
  PDAC    0.51   [0.21, 0.72]      35
  GC      0.34   [0.10, 0.54]      62

  cautions:      ptm_explain("IL6ST_N131", "TMX1_S270")
  glycoforms:    x$glycoforms
  cohort table:  x$cohorts
  all columns:   x$row
```

## Inspecting a result visually

In RStudio, `View(p$cohorts)` opens the estimates as a table. The installed example draws the intervals
already returned by the reader; it does not recompute the association.

```{r}
p <- ptm_pair("IL6ST_N131", "TMX1_S270")
source(system.file("examples", "inspect_pair.R", package = "ptmlink"))
plot_pair_cohorts(p)
```

For a gene-level view, `ptm_plot_network(ptm_network("EGFR", top_n = 15))` draws EGFR with its 15 strongest
partners as an undirected association network (requires `igraph`). The network export examples below create
files for Cytoscape.

## The reading rules as data

```{r}
e <- ptm_explain("TFRC_N727", "COIL_T303")
e[e$applies %in% TRUE, c("rule", "value", "threshold", "statement")]
ptm_explain(rows = head(g, 5))        # on rows already in hand, nothing fetched
```

Printed, the rules read as sentences. For `ptm_explain("IL6ST_N131", "TMX1_S270")`:

```
IL6ST_N131 x TMX1_S270
Applies:
  - Co-variation only: neither site is shown to regulate the other.
  - Significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction: q = 1.0e-04; evidence 5.9
    over 7 cohorts and 469 tumors.
  - Perturbation support, which admits a pair but never raises its rank.
    Channels: dose-response (the pair was measured together).
  - The program-adjusted 95% interval excludes zero (an annotation, never a
    ranking). Adjusted interval [0.09, 0.28].
Context:
  - This pair is in the top 2.4% of all scored site pairs measured in 7
    cohorts.
  - Without its most influential cohort (ccRCC), the pair keeps a larger share
    of its evidence than 99% of reported pairs measured in 7 cohorts.
Does not apply: same protein, parent-protein co-variation, self coupling,
  tissue composition, heterogeneity, one cohort, glycoform pooling,
  sequon ambiguity.

  full wording:  x$statement
```

Each row of the result is one rule on one pair: the column it reads, the threshold it is judged
against, whether it applies, and the sentence the website would show. The thresholds come from the
package reference, the one file that also drives the Python reader.

## Sites and where they sit

```{r}
s <- ptm_sites("EGFR")
s[, c("side", "site", "row_id", "position_canonical", "plddt", "residue_matches_model")]
```

Positions are on the UniProt canonical sequence, counted from the initiator methionine, the same
numbering the AlphaFold model uses. Coordinates are the alpha carbon in that model and pLDDT is the
model's own confidence; a distance between two sites is a fact about the model, never about coupling.

## The network of a gene

```{r}
net <- ptm_network("EGFR")
head(net[net$drawn, c("partner", "role", "n_site_pairs", "evidence_best", "rho_at_best")])
```

## A list of proteins or sites

`ptm_list()` takes a list from a differential analysis and answers, above all, which sites on the
other side of the pairs the list correlates with. Its level is `protein` when every entry is a gene.
When any entry is a site key the level is `site`: gene entries are expanded to their reported sites and
site entries stay as given. `level = "protein"` makes every site key contribute its protein instead. It returns `members` (how each entry resolved and is covered), `internal` (reported pairs
with a member on both sides and two different proteins),
`same_protein`, `neighbourhood` (a member on one side; the site on the other side is a partner site),
`partner_sites` (sites outside the list reached by more members than their reach among all significant pairs
predicts: of the N units on the members' side of the significant pairs the site pairs with K, the list holds n and
the site reaches x; a hypergeometric P per site, BH over all of them, the fold, the members reached
and the strongest pair in the view), `convergent` (the same test per partner protein), and
`connectivity` (significant pairs within the list against the number expected from the members' own numbers
of significant pairs, with a permutation P from degree-matched random lists). The row tables obey the
view. The three tests count the significant reported pairs (q < 0.05) between two different proteins; a pair
reported only for its perturbation support is not counted. `composition` says what share of each table is
labeled with a tissue-composition program on both sides, which a tumor-versus-normal list is
expected to be rich in.

```{r}
l <- ptm_list(c("EGFR", "ERBB2", "MET", "ITGB1", "CD44", "TFRC_N727"))
l                                           # the summary
l$members                                   # resolution, coverage, the named site
head(l$partner_sites)                       # site, protein, side, members reached, reach among reported pairs, fold, p, q, the best pair
head(l$convergent)                          # the same per partner protein
l$connectivity                              # observed, expected, ratio, permutation P
ptm_list(c("MAPK1_T185", "MAPK1_Y187", "STAT3_Y705"))   # a phosphosite list: the glycosites it converges on
```

The summary that `l` prints:

```

  site         side      members  fold      q  best evidence
  LAMB3_N810   glyco     9 of 53   9.0  0.010            5.6
  ITGA3_N605   glyco    14 of 53   4.8  0.010           11.6
  PHLDA2_S42   phospho   9 of 25   7.3  0.010            9.4

  members:           x$members

  plot:              ptm_plot_network(x)
```

An entry is a token: a pasted list is split on newlines, commas, semicolons and whitespace, and a
data.frame is read as entries in its first column. The tests say a site or
protein is reached by more members, or the list is more connected, than the members' degrees
predict. They say nothing about mechanism, kinases or pathways; the release carries none of those.
The website's List page runs the same two partner tests in the browser on the same significant pairs.
On the v1.0.0 release a list takes about 30 seconds and 7 GB of memory, and a query with narrow conditions about
10 seconds and a few GB. A query reads every pair its conditions match before the view and `limit` apply, so one
that matches more than a million pairs is refused unless `allow_full = TRUE`.

## Drawing and exporting a network

```{r}
g <- ptm_igraph(net)                                  # an undirected igraph graph, one edge per protein pair
ptm_plot_network(net)                                 # the partners marked drawn: width on evidence, orange with perturbation evidence, dashed when negative
ptm_plot_network(ptm_gene("EGFR", "glyco")[1:25, ], level = "site")
ptm_plot_network(l)                                   # a list's internal pairs
ptm_write_network(net, "egfr_network")                # egfr_network_nodes.tsv and _edges.tsv, for Cytoscape
ptm_write_network(l, "list_network", format = "graphml")
```

The graph is undirected because the statistic is symmetric; an edge at the gene level carries its
strongest site pair, as the website's network does. The layout carries no meaning.

## For agents

`ptm_tools()` turns the reference into tool descriptions: one per function marked as a tool, with a
JSON Schema for the arguments, the view's settings spelled out, and a `limit` on every function that
returns rows. Three shapes: Model Context Protocol, Anthropic and OpenAI. The repository's
`python/ptmlink_mcp.py` serves the same tools over stdio from the same file.

```{r}
t <- ptm_tools()                      # a list; attr(t, "instructions") is the release contract
cat(ptm_tools("openai", as = "json"))
```

## Reference and citation

```{r}
ptm_reference()$rules                 # the reading rules with their thresholds
ptm_reference(as = "json")            # the same as text, for a tool-description loader
ptm_cite()                            # the resource, its version and address
citation("ptmlink")
```

## What no function will do

Sort on the adjusted score, the parent-conditioned score or self-coupling; attach a
false-discovery rate to an adjusted column; let perturbation evidence raise a rank; state a
direction. Those are the release's rules, and the package holds to them.

## Reproducing the manuscript candidate screen

The full Parquet release and the complete candidate tables accompany the article. The installed example
uses the exact conjunction, including own-protein coupling below 0.6 on both sites, neither site labeled,
non-missing numerical fields, and retained-evidence percentile strictly above 0.5.

```{r}
source(system.file("examples", "candidate_screen.R", package = "ptmlink"))
rows <- arrow::read_parquet("path/to/release/site_served.parquet", col_select = tidyselect::all_of(candidate_columns))
candidates <- candidate_screen(rows)
perturbation_candidates <- candidates[candidates$anch_any %in% TRUE, ]
```

The screen does not exclude residual confounding or establish a mechanism; adjusted intervals have
no family-wide multiplicity correction.
